text:
Maya (CSM): quick pulse for helix this week — seeing sustained queue depth during PST night window, thought we should sync and flag any renewal risk.
Jon (CS Ops): saw the spike at ~02:10 UTC yesterday, queue depth hit ~42. baseline is usually <10.
Priya (Account Eng): thanks, Maya. do we have GPU-hour burn vs committed for helix?
Jon (CS Ops): committed 20k hrs/month. last 7 days they used ~5.6k (projected ~24k this month at current rate).
Maya (CSM): yikes that's ~20% over. renewal conversation next week — want concrete mitigations and a knob to offer.
Kaito (Infra): digging into tail latency — many jobs are small-batch sampling runs causing inefficient packing.
Kaito (Infra): snippet from the tracer:
```
rcli metrics tail --pool=reserved-helix --since=24h
avg_queue_depth: 12.4
p95_queue_depth: 38
p99_queue_depth: 45
avg_token_latency_ms: 87
p99_token_latency_ms: 420
```
Jon (CS Ops): also saw several short-lived pods that never filled their batch window, increasing per-token cost.
Priya (Account Eng): any quick config we can recommend to reduce burn? batching, prefix cache, or quota on ephemeral jobs?
Kaito (Infra): suggest 3 actions: 1) enable continuous batching with max_delay=15ms for sampling-heavy endpoints; 2) enforce a per-tenant concurrency cap for non-production keys; 3) enable prefix KV caching for the 2 large prompt families.
Maya (CSM): good. I'll propose those as negotiable operational credits for the renewal. need a rough estimate of expected % reduction.
Jon (CS Ops): based on similar customers, continuous batching + concurrency cap reduces GPU-hours ~18-25% for sampling-heavy workloads. with KV cache could add another 5-8%.
Priya (Account Eng): I'll draft the config playbook and a dry-run plan for Thursday night (off-peak) to test effect.
Maya (CSM): John's on-call tomorrow AM — Jon can you give a 1-line runbook for the customer to try so support can guide them?
Jon (CS Ops): 1-line: set environment var REDWOOD_BATCH_MODE=continuous, set REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=15, and apply per-tenant concurrency 6 for non-prod. we'll monitor queue depth for 48h.
Maya (CSM): perfect. I'll include that in the renewal pitch along with projected savings.
eric-bot: scheduled alert created: helix_reserved_pool_queue_depth > 30 for 10m -> notify #customer-success, #eng-runtime.
Priya (Account Eng): tagging deploy owners: @Kaito can you own the dry-run and collect cost/latency deltas?
Kaito (Infra): will run dry-run Thursday 23:00 UTC, will post results in this thread.
Maya (CSM): thanks all. action items: Priya — playbook & runbook, Kaito — dry-run, Jon — monitoring alert + baseline charts, Maya — renewal messaging + follow-up.
Jon (CS Ops): attaching quick chart link: https://dash.redwood.internal/helix/pool/reserved-queue?range=7d
Maya (CSM): next sync Friday EOD if we have numbers, otherwise I'll handle renewal convo with conservative estimate.
Priya (Account Eng): noted. will update Thursday night. :thumbsup:
Kaito (Infra): quick note: if the dry-run shows >30% improvement we can offer a 3-month credit as a remediation for the spike.
Maya (CSM): good plan. filing internal note with finance for provisional credit approval.
Jon (CS Ops): will keep the alerting window tight so we catch regressions.
Maya (CSM): closing for now — will post results. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
